caveats: The reference is a UNION of what the two listener transcripts (elevenlabs, gemini) surfaced to the judge — a shared benchmark for comparing configurations fairly; values neither listener transcribed sit outside its scope, so human spot-checks complement these numbers.
The judge and verifier are LLMs applying the written policy; their reference is unvalidated. Human ground truth remains the calibrator and will later score the judge itself.

Configs with a __gpt detector share a model family with the judge (detector luna, judge sol). Rule-verified precision especially may flatter them; the cross-family read (Gemini detector, GPT judge) is the cleaner comparison.
Value-based matching requires a shared category between reference item and interval; purely temporal matches do not.

metric_definitions.DETECTION RECALL: reference items matched by the config's intervals.json / all reference items (match = temporal IoU >= 0.3 or 70% cover, OR same canonicalized value within +/-2.5 s)
metric_definitions.DETECTION PRECISION: intervals matching a reference item / all intervals in intervals.json (same match rule, same reference)
metric_definitions.REDACTION RECALL: must-beep reference items covered by the rendered beeps / all must-beep items. An item counts as covered when a config interval matching it (detection match rule) is >= 95% beep-covered on the config's own clock, or when the reference spans themselves are >= 95% covered (channel-aware). The own-clock rule keeps cross-engine timestamp skew between the reference listeners and the config's engine from counting as leaks; items the config never detected are judged on reference-span coverage alone.
metric_definitions.LEAK RATE: 1 - redaction recall — the headline safety number
metric_definitions.POLICY-VERIFIED PRECISION (supplementary: intervals the adversarial verifier confirms satisfy a policy include rule / all intervals; reported alongside detection precision, never instead of it
